key_insight: G-PINNs improve PINN accuracy for shock-dominated PDEs by using a Gaussian spatial weighting that focuses training on high-gradient regions without needing prior shock-location knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed learning more practical for low-viscosity flow problems where shocks and discontinuities are hard to resolve with standard PINNs.
method: Apply a Gaussian-based spatially weighted loss to emphasize collocation points near steep solution gradients.
Let the PDE residual automatically identify and track moving discontinuities during training.
Test on 1D quasi-inviscid Burgers' equation for both stationary and moving shock cases.
evidence_signal: In the low-viscosity regime (ν = 0.0005), the method reduced L2 relative error to about 13% and 14%, versus 45% and 33% with standard PINNs for stationary and moving shocks, respectively.
watch_item: Performance may depend on tuning the Gaussian weighting strategy, and the approach is demonstrated only on 1D Burgers' shock problems.
paper_title: G-PINNs: Gaussian-based spatially weighted formulation for PINNs: 1D low-viscous Burgers
